Jordan Retail Workers Walk Out, Disrupting Operations Across Major Chains

Amman — Thousands of retail workers across Jordan walked off the job on Sunday, staging a nationwide strike that has disrupted operations at dozens of supermarkets, department stores, and shopping centers. The Jordan Retail Workers’ Union called the action in protest against stagnant wages and what it described as “unsafe and exhausting working conditions” following months of unsuccessful negotiations with employers.

Major chains, including CityMart, Al-Madina Stores, and Jordan Value Shop, reported that many of their branches were shuttered or operating with skeleton staff as of Monday afternoon. Long lines formed at open outlets, with customers facing limited service and empty shelves. The union estimated that over 70% of retail workers in Amman, Irbid, and Zarqa joined the walkout, affecting more than 250 retail sites nationwide.

“Our members are demanding fair compensation and safer work environments. The retail sector has seen rising profits, but workers have not benefited,” union spokesperson Samer Al-Khatib told reporters outside CityMart’s Amman flagship store, where several hundred employees gathered in protest.

Industry analysts say the strike is the largest industrial action in Jordan’s retail sector in over a decade. “The immediate impact is a significant loss of daily revenue for retailers, and if the strike continues, the effects could intensify,” said Laila Haddad, an analyst at Amman Financial Research.

Retail companies have urged workers to return, stating that negotiations are ongoing. “We respect our employees’ rights and are committed to reaching a fair solution,” a spokesperson for Jordan Value Shop said.

The strike remained in effect as of early Tuesday. The union has not announced an end date, and further negotiations are expected this week. Retailers continue to monitor store operations and customer service levels amid ongoing disruptions.
